avoid: Explicit lyrics in cumbia villera tracks
children.game_version: Musical statues using the stop-start nature of cumbia breaks.

seniors.seated_version: Gentle side-to-side torso sways and hand-clapping to the 4/4 rhythm.
seniors.standing_version: Small side-steps with a focus on steady balance; avoid rapid turns.
seniors.tempo_and_range: Use slower romantic cumbia tracks (e.g., Gilda) to reduce cardiovascular strain.

movement_profile.formation_and_space: Large dance halls (bailantas) and social party spaces
movement_profile.partnering: Commonly danced as a couple in a social setting
movement_profile.tempo_feel: Varies from slow romantic ballads to fast-paced electronic beats

music_profile.musical_form: Verse-chorus structure often featuring instrumental solos (accordion or keyboard)
music_profile.rhythm_pattern: Constant güiro scrape and electronic percussion with syncopated basslines
music_profile.sound_description: A dense mix of electronic synthesizers and traditional tropical percussion, often featuring a bright accordion or a sharp electric guitar lead over a steady, driving cumbia beat.
music_profile.vocal_style: Charged with vocal harmonies; ranges from romantic/sensual to aggressive/explicit

teaching.formation: Social partner dance or group dancing in halls
teaching.level_notes: Accessible to all social classes; primarily a social party dance.
teaching.rhythm: Cumbia rhythm (2/4 or 4/4 feel with heavy emphasis on the offbeat)
